Subject: Third-party subprocessors & data residency - post-call recap

Hi Sarah 

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side related to the data handling topics you raised:

Summary of your asks:
- Confirmation of where customer data (and telemetry) are stored and processed (US vs EU).
- List of third-party subprocessors (telemetry vendors, cloud providers, marketplace partners) and their data access scopes.
- PII classification & retention defaults (and how they can be configured).
- Logging and audit controls (who can access logs, retention, and redaction).

What I'm sharing now: redacted_subprocessors_list.pdf (attached)

Includes our cloud provider, telemetry provider, and marketplace partners. Separate note: our hosted offering stores data in region-specific clusters; Dedicated/Private options can be configured for on-prem or VPC-based residency.

Requested next steps from Acme:
1) Confirm which residency region(s) you need (US-only, EU-only, hybrid).
2) Share any minimum retention requirements or PII categories that must be excluded from logs.
3) If you want, we can set up a short handoff with Security (Marcus) to walk through SOC2 artifacts and logging controls.

I've attached the redacted subprocessor list and a first-pass redline of the MSA for your legal team to review. Happy to jump on another call this week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa 

This is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side after reviewing the redacted list:

1) Residency: Acme Health requires US-only processing for PHI-adjacent data. Can you confirm whether your hosted clusters can be restricted to US regions only and whether telemetry sent to your vendors can be prevented from leaving the US?

2) Telemetry vendors: we need the exact vendor names and whether telemetry contains any PII/hashable identifiers. If telemetry includes hashed user IDs, we may need strict retention windows or an opt-out.

3) Logs & access: who at Redwood and at third parties can access request/response logs? Is there per-team IAM and audit logging for access to logs?

We'd also like to get a copy of your SOC 2 Type II report and any relevant penetration test summaries (redacted). Could Marcus or your security lead join a follow-up call to walk our DPO through controls?

Best,
Sarah Jones
Director of Product Security | Acme Health
sarah.jones@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Third-party subprocessors & data residency - post-call recap

Hi Sarah 

Appreciate the clear list. Answers below and next steps:

1) Residency: Hosted clusters can be restricted by customer to US-only regions. For telemetry, we have configuration toggles: telemetry can be routed only to US-based vendors or disabled for a given customer. Dedicated and Private deployments guarantee data never leaves the customer VPC/region.

2) Telemetry vendors: attached redacted_subprocessors_list.pdf includes vendor names and data access scopes. Short list (redacted):
- Primary cloud: Redwood Cloud (managed on AWS us-east-1/us-west-2)
- Telemetry: TimberLog (logging/metrics)
- Marketplace partners: DataVizCo (optional analytics integration)

We do not include raw PII in telemetry by default. Telemetry may contain hashed or pseudonymous IDs for usage correlation; we can disable or truncate those fields per-customer. Retention: default telemetry retention is 90 days; can be shortened to meet Acme policy.

3) Logs & access: Access to request/response logs is restricted to a small set of SRE and Security engineers via role-based IAM. Third-party vendors have scoped access (e.g., telemetry provider sees aggregated logs only) and are contractually prohibited from using data for model training. All access is audited.

Attachments: redacted_subprocessors_list.pdf (contains vendor names + access scopes) and a redline of the proposed MSA. I'll also share our SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary via a secure link once Marcus confirms readiness to share.

Next steps: Marcus, can you join a 30-min call with Acme DPO (cc'd) next week to walk through SOC2 and logging controls? Neha, I'll need the HUBSpot record updated and a follow-up cadence set for 2 weeks.

Thanks,
Marissa
Attachment: redacted_subprocessors_list.pdf (pdf)

Happy to join. Quick notes ahead of the call:
